loadouts.lore: A practical security issue copied from isolated stations that cannot expect prompt naval help. Reliable Rooks fill the racks while each fire-team lead receives the one pulse rifle worth entrusting to a trained hand.

Recovered Pather assault tables favor violent entry over a sustained firing line. Breaching carbines, improvised demolition tools, and scarce anti-armor weapons turn ordinary compartments into close, decisive killing grounds.

Fleet line doctrine assumes disciplined volleys, organic marksmen, and enough smoke to keep a stalled advance moving. It is expensive to sustain on the frontier but reassuringly familiar to academy-trained officers.
A modern boarding package for breaking defended rooms before the enemy can reorganize. Shredder teams open the breach while a single Shattercap carrier holds the answer to massed soft targets.

This scarce support establishment gives every fire team a marksman, an automatic weapon, and access to ship-killing hardware cut down for ground use. Few independent companies can replace its losses quickly.
Vac-rated workwear and scavenged militia plate form the baseline protection of cash-poor companies. The leaders wear the armor because someone must still be standing when the section loses direction.
A mixed protection schedule descended from refinery guards and planetary auxiliaries. It spends proper scout plate where mobility matters and accepts conspicuous gaps everywhere else.
Fleet combat protection concentrates dependable laminate around the marines expected to take and hold the contact line. Rear billets trade some protection for the mobility needed to exploit a breach.

Low-profile scout plate was designed for teams that must see the enemy, survive the first exchange, and disappear before heavier forces arrive. Militia backing keeps the schedule attainable outside a naval depot.
